The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[-6,4].$ The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. It consists of three line segments and the arc of a semicircle with radius $2.$ If $f(-3)=5,$ calculate $f(4).$

$f(4)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the fundamental theorem of calculus, we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-f(-3) \\ {\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-5 \\ f(4) & =5+{\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that the integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis.

The graph consists of $2$ parts on $[-3,4]:$ the arc of the semicircle for $x\in [-3,1]$ and the line segments for $x\in [1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The first integral ${A}_{1}$ represents the signed area between the semicircle and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,1].$ Since the semicircle has radius $2,$ the area is half the area of a circle of radius $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The second integral ${A}_{2}$ represents the signed area between the line segments and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of the integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =2\pi +4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the value of the integral, we can find $f(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =5+{\int }_{-3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =5+(2\pi +4) \\  & =2\pi +9\end{aligned}
$$
